mutants.description: PWM polarity misremembered as active-low: the switching period is taken from falling edge to falling edge and the duty snapshot is taken on the rising edge, so duty_count measures the low (LS) phase instead of HS conduction.
mutants.reason: For any running PWM with duty other than 50%, duty_count reports the low-phase length (period minus high time) instead of the high-phase length; prev_period stays about the same, so the host infers the wrong Vout.

mutants.description: The start-of-cycle detector fires on any PWM edge rather than only the rising edge, so the period counter is restarted at the end of HS conduction as well.
mutants.reason: With a running PWM, prev_period alternately captures the high-phase and the low-phase length instead of the full period, and duty_count is never updated by a normal falling edge because the restart branch wins.

mutants.description: A rising edge that ends a saturated (stalled) period is treated as invalid and does not update prev_period, so the all-ones out-of-range marker is never exported.
mutants.reason: After pwm_sync stalls long enough for period_counter to saturate and then resumes, prev_period keeps the last plausible period instead of reading all-ones, hiding the stall from the host.

mutants.description: The saturation test looks ahead at the next count, so the period counter stops one short at all-ones minus one instead of reaching the all-ones out-of-range marker.
mutants.reason: When pwm_sync stalls for more than 254 clocks, the following rising edge exports prev_period = 0xFE (and a fall exports duty_count = 0xFE) instead of the all-ones value the host recognises as out-of-range.

mutants.description: When a stalled-high PWM finally falls, the saturated period counter is restarted at the fall as if measurement had recovered, rather than held until the next rising edge.
mutants.reason: After a stall-high long enough to saturate the counter, the next rising edge exports only the low-phase length as prev_period, a plausible short period, instead of the all-ones marker for the stalled cycle.

mutants.description: The duty snapshot is taken on the PWM low level instead of on the falling edge, so duty_count keeps being overwritten throughout the low phase.
mutants.reason: For a running PWM, duty_count follows period_counter during the whole low phase and ends near the full period length at the next rise, instead of holding the high-phase length captured at the fall.

mutants.description: The falling-edge clock is counted as part of HS conduction, so duty_count is one higher than the count taken from the same counter run for prev_period.
mutants.reason: For every normal period, duty_count reads one count higher than the high-phase length on the same basis as prev_period, so duty/period is biased high and reads 100% duty one count early.
